subject: Freeing a few of many constrained intercepts in two-group invariance testing

messages.author: a8a90dd3e8666575
messages.subject: Freeing a few of many constrained intercepts in two-group invariance testing
parts:
Hi lavaan group,

I am running a two-group measurement invariance investigation. I have 3 latent factors, each of which has 9 indictors (total number indictors is 27). I am using the 'group.equal' option to constrain all loadings and intercepts (see code below). My data passed the metric invariance test (i.e., 24 constrained factor loadings only). Next I assess scalar invariance by also constraining the intercepts to be equal across the two groups (see code below). Constraining all 24 intercepts significantly degrades model fit. So I want to assess partial scalar invariance.

I used lavTestScore(fit3m, cumulative = T) and note there are only 3 of 24 intercepts where freeing the cross-group constraints would yield large chi-square values.

QUESTION: How can I free 3 specific intercept constraints while maintaining the remaining 21 constraints?

Any advice will be much appreciated,
Jason

M0Y CODE
model1 <- '
 NFCf =~  N4r + N5r + N9r + N3r + N11 + N13 + N2 + N10 + N12r
 EXPf =~  R13 + R26 + R31 + R8 + R34 + R35 + R22 + R24r + R33
 DDf  =~  D8  + D28 + D31 + D14 + D17 + D20 + D2 + D5 + D25
'
fit3m <- lavaan::cfa(model = model1, data = df, group="FORM",  meanstructure=T,
                     estimator = "ML", missing = "listwise", check.post=T, mimic = "lavaan",
                     std.lv = F, std.ov = F, test = "standard", se = "standard",
                     group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))

messages.author: ff3a366aa7a9b488
messages.subject: Re: Freeing a few of many constrained intercepts in two-group invariance testing
parts: You can use the group.partial argument to freely estimate one or more parameters: https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

messages.subject: Re: Freeing a few of many constrained intercepts in two-group invariance testing
parts: You can use the group.partial argument to freely estimate one or more parameters: https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

You can also specify it in your syntax.

N4r ~ c(NA, NA, NA)*1
